label: Suffering-adjusted days per animal (Ambitious Impact, via ACE)

rows.label: SADs averted per hen-year moved from a battery cage to an aviary

source.title: Ambitious Impact SADs, via ACE's Sinergia Animal CEA (2025), 'SADs per animal' tab
source.quote: 28.9 SADs for a battery-caged hen minus 11.5 for an aviary hen

rows.explainer:
How much suffering one laying hen is spared for each year she lives in an aviary instead of a battery cage, in suffering-adjusted days (SADs): days of suffering weighted by pain intensity and by the hen's welfare range.

Best guess: Ambitious Impact's current figures as ACE used them in 2025 (28.9 − 11.5 = 17.49). Low end: the 7.93 ACE used in its 2025 review of The Humane League for the same transition, from an older version of the SAD figures. ACE's own models disagree by 2×, so models that use this fact carry that disagreement as uncertainty.

rows.label: SADs averted per hen-year moved from an enriched cage to an aviary

source.title: ACE, The Humane League CEA (2025), Cage-Free Accountability tab
source.quote: Assumes hens are being moved from a 'furnished' or 'enriched' cage into an aviary.

rows.explainer:
The same as the cage-to-aviary figure, for hens starting in 'enriched' (furnished) cages, as in the EU since 2012. Smaller because enriched cages are less bad.

The range (half to double) is ours: ACE gives a point value, and the cage-to-aviary figure moved by 2× between ACE's own models.

rows.label: SADs averted per broiler chicken raised under Better Chicken Commitment standards

source.title: ACE, The Humane League CEA (2025), BCC Accountability tab

rows.explainer:
Suffering averted over one broiler chicken's life (about six weeks) when it is raised to Better Chicken Commitment / European Chicken Commitment standards: slower-growing breeds, more space, enrichment and better slaughter.

ACE uses 0.64 in several 2025 reviews. The range (half to double) is ours; ACE gives no range and notes its SAD values have since been updated.

rows.label: SADs averted per animal-product meal replaced by a plant-based meal

source.title: ACE, Sinergia Animal CEA (2025), meat reduction tab: 900,203 SADs (86,972–1,713,434) for 997,510 meals

rows.explainer:
Suffering averted when one meal with meat, fish, eggs or dairy is replaced by a plant-based one, through the animals that are no longer bred and raised for it. It depends heavily on what the meal would have contained: a chicken or fish meal involves many more animal-days of suffering than a beef meal.

Best guess and high end: ACE's 2025 Sinergia Animal estimate (0.90 per meal, upper bound 1.72). Low end: the 0.084 ACE used for Sociedade Vegetariana Brasileira's institutional meals in the same year. ACE's own figures differ by 10×, so use a model-specific value only when the charity reports what the replaced meals contained, and say why.

Reference meal: the best guess averages Sinergia's institutional canteen meals across the countries it works in, whose per-country values differ several-fold with the meat species served. To adapt it, scale by the ratio of the charity's meat per meal and species mix to that reference, as input rows with sources.

rows.label: Animals spared per animal-product meal replaced

source.title: ACE, Sociedade Vegetariana Brasileira CEA (2025), Institutional meat reduction tab

rows.explainer: How many animals are no longer raised for each meal replaced. Context only: SADs, not animal counts, are the comparable outcome. Range is ours, roughly halving for beef-heavy diets and up to ACE's other estimates for chicken- and fish-heavy diets.

rows.label: Fall in production per unit fall in consumption (cumulative elasticity factor)

source.title: Norwood and Lusk (2011), Compassion, by the Pound, figure 8.2, as reproduced by Brian Tomasik

rows.explainer:
When someone eats one pound less chicken, prices fall a little and other people buy a little more, so total consumption, and therefore production, falls by less than a pound. Norwood and Lusk estimate 0.76 lb for chicken, 0.74 for pork, 0.68 for beef, 0.56 for milk and 0.91 eggs per egg.

Best guess is chicken's, since chickens and fish dominate the animal count of a typical replaced meal; the range spans milk (0.56) to eggs (0.91). Diet-change models multiply by this; ACE's models don't, which is one reason charityevals' diet-change results can run lower than ACE's.

rows.label: SADs averted per farmed shrimp electrically stunned before slaughter instead of chilled alive in ice slurry

source.title: Ambitious Impact SAD inputs for shrimp stunning, via ACE's Aquatic Life Institute CEA (2024), 'SADs Estimate' tab; durations from McKay & McAuliffe (2024), Rethink Priorities, appendix p. 28
source.cell: SADs Estimate!B7 (stun success 0.97), B12 (sentience 0.3), B13 (welfare range 0.62), B16 (result 0.097, formula (B14+B15)*B7*B12*B13*3.18); comparative rating to disabling pain row (excruciating 11.85)
source.quote: Likelihood of shrimp sentience 30% ... Welfare range of shrimps 62%

rows.explainer:
Suffering one farmed shrimp is spared when it is electrically stunned (unconscious within about a second) instead of being chilled alive in an ice slurry, in suffering-adjusted days (SADs): one SAD is one human-equivalent day of disabling pain, so pain time is weighted by intensity and by the animal's moral weight. It counts only the slaughter; harvest, transport and life on the farm are unchanged.

Method: Ambitious Impact's (AIM) 2024 (version 1) shrimp-stunning calculation, as ACE used it for Aquatic Life Institute, with one input replaced. AIM v1 computes SADs = (disabling-equivalent days from ice slurry + from fear) × 0.97 (share of shrimp the stunner knocks out, from an Optimar/Tesco case study) × 0.3 (probability shrimp are sentient) × 0.62 (welfare range) × 3.18, with excruciating pain weighted 11.85 times disabling pain. The ×3.18 was AIM's v1 cross-species convention for 'the exponential growth of the comparative rating of the pain types': ACE's 2025 Sinergia Animal sheet, the source of the hen fact above, applies it to AIM's pig figures with the same note (ACE's note adds that AIM 'leans towards overestimating' with it). We deliberately stay on AIM v1, so shrimp are valued on the same basis as the site's other SAD facts, which come from ACE's 2025 sheets built on v1. AIM replaced this method with SADs v2 in early 2026 (https://research.ambitiousimpact.com/ambitious-impact-eval/suffering-adjusted-days-methodology): v2 has no ×3.18, lowers shrimp's moral weight to about 0.083 (welfare range 0.2 × sentience 0.416, against v1's 0.19) and uses about 4.8 minutes of slaughter pain citing Rethink Priorities; on v2 the figure is about 0.0008 SADs per shrimp, 6.8 times below our best. When the site's SAD facts move to v2, this one should move with them. The ×3.18 scales every pain level equally, so the excruciating-to-disabling ratio stays AIM's 11.85, at the low end of Rethink Priorities' 5–1000.

The input we replace is the duration. AIM assumes 20 minutes of excruciating pain, citing the Global Seafood Alliance; that is the recommended minimum time in the slurry to stop all movement, an upper bound for the slowest animals. We use Rethink Priorities' estimate for ice-slurry slaughter instead (McKay & McAuliffe 2024, https://rethinkpriorities.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/06/Quantifyingandprioritizingshrimpwelfarethreats.pdf, appendix p. 28, Slaughter row: 6 s–2 min, mean 48 s, excruciating; 23.7 s–7.9 min, mean 3.16 min, disabling).

Best guess: (48 s × 11.85 + 190 s) ÷ 86,400 s = 0.0088 disabling-equivalent days, plus AIM's fear term scaled from 20 to about 4 minutes (0.001), × 0.97 × 0.3 × 0.62 × 3.18 = 0.0056 SADs per shrimp.

Range. The excruciating-to-disabling weight is the largest judgment inside this figure. High end 0.1: AIM's unmodified figure (0.097, with its 20 minutes), which is above Rethink Priorities' own framework with its mean weight (uniform 5–1000, mean 502: 0.051 with AIM's moral weight and no ×3.18), and which allows for producers whose alternative is slower death by asphyxiation in air. Low end 0.0005: about a minute of pain (sub-zero slurry, where insensibility comes faster) at AIM's weights without the ×3.18, close to AIM v2's own figure (0.0008). Rethink Priorities' sentience-adjusted welfare range for shrimp (median 0.031, 95th percentile 1.15; Fischer 2023, https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/Qk3hd6PrFManj8K6o/rethink-priorities-welfare-range-estimates) is lower than AIM's 0.3 × 0.62 = 0.19 at the median and higher in its tail; we keep AIM's for comparability.
